diagnostic_evidence.quote: The real-valued spherical harmonics form an orthonormal basis of $L^2(\S^2)$.

issues.failure_explanation: For m<0 the displayed real spherical harmonic is (|m|\varphi), which is not periodic, not an eigenfunction of the spherical Laplacian, and not part of the stated orthonormal basis. The labelled eigenvalue identity and the basis property therefore fail as written.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the negative-m branch by the standard real spherical harmonic definition (a real linear combination of complex spherical harmonics) so that the orthonormal basis and eigenfunction identities hold.
issues.overall_effect: Every spectral expansion, moment computation, regularity estimate, and convergence proof that uses the real spherical harmonics is unsupported as written.
issues.title: Incorrect negative-m real spherical harmonic definition
issues.why_classification: A local correction to the standard definition restores the intended setting; no new proof architecture or loss of advertised rates is required.

issues.failure_explanation: The coefficient mean is E[L_{\ell,m}(t)] = t\meanlm, while the variance is t\varlm. Hence E[|L_{\ell,m}(t)|^2] = t\varlm + t^2\meanlm^2, not t(\varlm+\meanlm^2). The displayed equality in the assumption is false for nonzero mean.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the displayed equality to t\sum (1+\ell(\ell+1))^\eta \varlm + t^2\sum (1+\ell(\ell+1))^\eta \meanlm^2, or state the finite-sum condition as a sufficient inequality with the correct mean term.
issues.overall_effect: The regularity condition stated as equivalent to L^2(\Omega,H^\eta) convergence is incorrect for nonzero-mean Lévy processes; the assumption as written is incompatible with the paper's nonzero-mean setting.
issues.title: Wrong second-moment scaling in Assumption StrongLevyProcess
issues.why_classification: The repair is a local moment-scaling correction; the intended regularity hypotheses and downstream conclusions survive.

issues.failure_explanation: For square-integrable Lévy processes, mean and variance are linear in time. The assumption states constant mean and variance in t for the processes \hat L_{\ell,m}, which is false for all t unless the process is degenerate.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State E[\hat L_{\ell,m}(t)] = t\hatmean and Var(\hat L_{\ell,m}(t)) = t\hatvar (or define \hatmean,\hatvar as per-unit-time quantities and add the t factors).
issues.overall_effect: The special Lévy process setting is mis-specified; the per-unit-time constants used later for rates are not actually assumed.
issues.title: Missing time scaling in Assumption SpecialLevyProcess
issues.why_classification: Adding the standard t factors is a local correction that preserves the intended special setting and rates.

issues.failure_explanation: The L^2 norm of the deterministic tail is bounded by e^{-(\kappa+1)(\kappa+2)t}\|\E[X^0]\| (or the weaker e^{-(\kappa+1)^2 t}), not by e^{-2(\kappa+1)^2 t}\|\E[X^0]\|; the proof line has not taken the square root of the squared exponential decay.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the proof line to the norm-level exponential bound e^{-(\kappa+1)^2 t}\|\E[X^0]\|, matching the statement.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of the mean-error bound in the spectral corollary contains an invalid calculation step.
issues.title: Incorrect deterministic tail exponent in Corollary L:SA2 proof
issues.why_classification: The statement is unaffected and the proof step is a local exponent correction.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: for all $\rho < \eta + 1/m$, the error is bounded by

issues.failure_explanation: The weak theorem gives rate \kappa^{-(\beta+\rho)} for the test-function regularity \rho. The corollary's first display claims \kappa^{-2(\eta+1)} for all polynomial-growth test functions without fixing \rho=\eta+1 (and without tying p=2m). Its second display uses \eta+1/m, which requires p=2m, but the stated hypothesis only assumes some NoMeanLevyProcess p.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the corollary to test functions with \rho=\eta+1 in the first two settings and specify p=2m in the general setting, or state the supported rate \kappa^{-(\eta+1+\rho)} with \rho<\eta+2/p.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised weak convergence rates are broader than supported; the guaranteed rate depends on \rho and on the relation between the polynomial degree m and the L^p integrability p.
issues.title: Weak corollary overclaims rates and omits p/m relation
issues.why_classification: A supported repair requires limiting the test-function class and adding a nontrivial hypothesis connection, but it avoids new global architecture and preserves a comparable weak-rate result.

issues.failure_explanation: The discrete approximation is the step function with weight \xi^{k-j+\delta} on [t_{j-1},t_j]. The written exponent k-(\underline{s}+1)h^{-1}+\delta is not that weight (it adds 1/h and is not an integer step index), so the integral representation and the subsequent variance bound are not valid as written.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the integrand by e^{-\ell(\ell+1)(t_k-s)} - \xi^{k-j(s)+\delta} with j(s) the grid index, or return directly to the sum over j used in the scheme.
issues.overall_effect: The proof step comparing the stochastic integral to the Euler--Maruyama increments is unsupported.
issues.title: Ill-defined step-function weight in Thm:ConvEM proof
issues.why_classification: The correction is a local indexing/notation repair of the proof step; the theorem statement does not require new architecture.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof of the second-moment error displays a product of two large parentheses with plus signs that does not follow from the algebraic identity |a^2-b^2| = |a-b||a+b| applied to the moment formulas. The subsequent bounding steps are therefore unsupported, and the claimed h^{\min\{\beta,1\}} second-moment rate is not derived.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Recompute the second-moment difference directly from \eqref{eq:second-moment_spectral} and \eqref{eq:second-mom_EM}, then bound the exponential and integral-approximation terms using Proposition~\ref{prop:AuxExp}; this is a contained but nontrivial proof repair.
issues.overall_effect: The second-moment convergence statement in the fully discrete theorem is not established as written.
issues.title: Invalid second-moment algebra in Thm:ConvEM2 proof
issues.why_classification: The repair requires a new local estimate and correction of the proof algebra, but it does not need new global architecture and the stated theorem is plausibly recoverable.

issues.failure_explanation: The theorem gives h^{\min\{\beta/2,1\}} with \beta<\alpha/2 under the special Lévy assumption. For \alpha<2 this only yields rates h^{\alpha/4-\varepsilon}, not the endpoint h^{\alpha/4}; the prose claims the theorem supports h^{\min\{\alpha/4,1/2\}} directly.

failure_location.quote: confirm the expected convergence rate of $h^{\min\{\alpha/4,1/2\}}$ from Theorem~\ref{Thm:ConvEM}.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate the expected rate as h^{\min\{\beta/2,1\}} with \beta<\alpha/2, or as arbitrarily close to h^{\min\{\alpha/4,1\}} where the cap applies.
issues.overall_effect: The numerical discussion misstates the strong time-discretization rate guaranteed by the theory.
issues.title: Numerical prose overstates time-discretization rate
issues.why_classification: The fix is a local prose correction of the rate statement; the formal theorem is unchanged.

issues.failure_explanation: With \beta=\eta+1, the theorem's mean-error exponent is \min\{1,(\beta+1)/2\}=\min\{1,(\eta+2)/2\}. For \eta=-1 this is 1/2 and for \eta=-1/2 it is 3/4, not 1. Thus O(h) is not guaranteed for the listed negative regularity cases.

failure_location.quote: According to Theorem~\ref{Thm:ConvEM2}, we expect a convergence rate of order $h$ in time.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State the expected rate as h^{\min\{1,(\eta+2)/2\}}, or restrict the O(h) claim to \eta\ge 0.
issues.overall_effect: The numerical expectations for the mean error are inconsistent with the theorem for \eta<0.
issues.title: Numerical prose claims O(h) mean rate for negative eta
issues.why_classification: The correction is a local rate statement in the prose; no formal theorem needs to be abandoned.
